The player must first find white wool in the environment, then use that knowledge/resource to build a road. This creates a logical multi-hop sequence: locating the building material is a prerequisite to constructing the road. Both tasks are observable and verifiable - finding wool requires visual identification, and building a road requires placing blocks in a linear pattern.

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task — the player must navigate near the white wool pile and face it to visually identify it. Target is the center of the 3x3+1 wool pile at spawn-relative (4, 0, 4). Max distance 5 blocks ensures the player actually approaches the pile rather than just spawning nearby, and facing_tolerance 60° confirms they are looking at it.

Uses count_in_box_at_least(kind='block', object='white_wool', min_count=5) because this is a build/place task — the player must place white wool blocks to form a road. The detection box covers x=-10 to x=2, y=0, z=-10 to z=10 (spawn-relative), which intentionally EXCLUDES x=3-5 where the pre-existing wool pile sits (9 blocks at x=3-5, z=3-5 plus 1 at x=4,y=1,z=4). This ensures only newly player-placed blocks are counted. The box is generous (±10 XZ) to allow the player to build the road anywhere in the western/central portion of the platform. Min_count=5 represents a minimal but recognizable road segment.
